## Briefing

::: {.rq-lesson}
**Welcome to Region 1.** No statistics yet: just the habits that make every later analysis work. Read first: [Getting Started](../r-foundations/getting-started.qmd).
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
bp <- c(118, 126, 140, 132)      # a numeric vector
bp[2]                            # R counts from 1
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 126
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
sex <- factor(c("Male", "Female", "Female"))
levels(sex)                      # sorted alphabetically: the first is the reference
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Female" "Male"  
```


:::
:::


::: {.rq-lesson}
**Objects and types.** `<-` stores a value under a name. Numbers in quotes are text, and text cannot be averaged. A **factor** is a categorical variable; its first level is the reference in models.
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# the start of every script
library(tidyverse)                         # load packages (install once, load every session)
ncd <- read_csv("data/ncd_survey.csv")     # path relative to the RStudio Project
glimpse(ncd)                               # rows, columns and the type of each column
```
:::


::: {.rq-lesson}
**Projects and scripts.** Work inside an **RStudio Project** so paths like `data/ncd_survey.csv` work on any computer (no `setwd()`). Write everything in a **script**, never only in the console, and never overwrite the raw data.
:::

## Level 1 · Objects and types {.rq-level}


::: {.rq-item data-id="b1-02" data-world="b1" data-type="mcq" data-diff="2" data-tags="r-objects" data-hash="vl0goo.fr1tjj" data-show="VGhlIGFnZXMgYXJlIHN0b3JlZCBhcyB0ZXh0LCBzbyB0aGVyZSBpcyBub3RoaW5nIHRvIGF2ZXJhZ2U=" data-explain="VGhlIHF1b3RlcyBtYWtlIGVhY2ggdmFsdWUgYSBjaGFyYWN0ZXIgc3RyaW5nLiBDb252ZXJ0IHdpdGggYXMubnVtZXJpYygpIGZpcnN0LCBvciBmaXggdGhlIGltcG9ydCBzbyB0aGUgY29sdW1uIGlzIHJlYWQgYXMgbnVtYmVycy4=" data-hints="WyJMb29rIGF0IHRoZSBxdW90YXRpb24gbWFya3MuIl0="}
```r
ages <- c("45", "52", "38")
mean(ages)
#> [1] NA
#> Warning: argument is not numeric or logical: returning NA
```
Why does this fail?

- A vector needs at least five values before mean() can work on it
- One of the ages is missing, so the mean cannot be calculated
- mean() works on data frames, so the vector has to be wrapped first
- The ages are stored as text, so there is nothing to average
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="b1-03" data-world="b1" data-type="num" data-diff="1" data-tags="r-objects" data-dp="0" data-hashes="b9h7cu.dbg15k" data-show="MjU4" data-explain="UiBjb3VudHMgZnJvbSAxLCBzbyBicFsyXSBpcyAxMjYgYW5kIGJwWzRdIGlzIDEzMjsgMTI2ICsgMTMyID0gMjU4Lg==" data-hints="WyJQb3NpdGlvbiAxIGhvbGRzIHRoZSBmaXJzdCB2YWx1ZSwgbm90IHBvc2l0aW9uIDAuIl0="}

```r
bp[2] + bp[4]
```
What does this print? (whole number)
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="b1-04" data-world="b1" data-type="mcq" data-diff="2" data-tags="factors" data-hash="vl1762.fr2mi9" data-show="UnVyYWwsIGJlY2F1c2UgbGV2ZWxzIGFyZSBzb3J0ZWQgYWxwaGFiZXRpY2FsbHkgYnkgZGVmYXVsdA==" data-explain="VW5sZXNzIHlvdSBzZXQgbGV2ZWxzIHlvdXJzZWxmLCBmYWN0b3IoKSBzb3J0cyB0aGVtIGFscGhhYmV0aWNhbGx5LCBzbyBSdXJhbCBjb21lcyBmaXJzdCBhbmQgYmVjb21lcyB0aGUgcmVmZXJlbmNlLiBVc2UgZmFjdG9yKHgsIGxldmVscyA9IGMoLi4uKSkgdG8gY2hvb3NlLg==" data-hints="WyJIb3cgZG9lcyBSIG9yZGVyIHRleHQgaWYgeW91IGRvIG5vdCB0ZWxsIGl0IG90aGVyd2lzZT8iXQ=="}
```r
res <- factor(c("Urban", "Rural", "Urban"))
levels(res)
```
Which level comes first, and so becomes the reference level in a model?

- Urban, because it is the most frequent value in the vector
- Neither; R treats the two levels as unordered with no reference
- Urban, because it is the first value that appears in the data
- Rural, because levels are sorted alphabetically by default
:::

## Level 2 · Projects and packages {.rq-level}


::: {.rq-item data-id="b1-01" data-world="b1" data-type="mcq" data-diff="1" data-tags="projects" data-hash="vl03fz.fr1f26" data-show="UGF0aHMgYmVjb21lIHJlbGF0aXZlIHRvIHRoZSBwcm9qZWN0LCBzbyBpdCBydW5zIG9uIGFueSBjb21wdXRlcg==" data-explain="QSBwcm9qZWN0IHNldHMgdGhlIHdvcmtpbmcgZm9sZGVyIGZvciB5b3UsIHNvIHBhdGhzIGxpa2UgZGF0YS9uY2Rfc3VydmV5LmNzdiB3b3JrIG9uIGFueW9uZSdzIG1hY2hpbmUuIHNldHdkKCkgaGFyZC1jb2RlcyBvbmUgY29tcHV0ZXIncyBmb2xkZXJzLg==" data-hints="WyJUaGluayBhYm91dCB3aGF0IGhhcHBlbnMgd2hlbiBhIGNvbGxlYWd1ZSBvcGVucyB5b3VyIHNjcmlwdCBvbiB0aGVpciBsYXB0b3AuIl0="}
Why is it worth opening your analysis as an RStudio Project rather than calling setwd() at the top of the script?

- The project installs every package your script needs automatically
- It stops other people from opening or changing your script
- R runs noticeably faster when it is opened through a project file
- Paths become relative to the project, so it runs on any computer
:::

You installed dplyr last week. Today, in a fresh R session, filter(ncd, age > 50) gives: could not find function "filter". What is the most likely cause?

- The package is installed but has not been loaded in this session
- The package was removed from your computer when R was closed
- R needs the data to be sorted by age before it can be filtered
- The function only works on files that were saved as Excel sheets
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="b1-06" data-world="b1" data-type="order" data-diff="1" data-tags="projects,import" data-hash="xkwsiu.n0j2ef" data-show="" data-explain="UHJvamVjdCBmaXJzdCwgdGhlbiB0aGUgZGF0YSBpbiBwbGFjZSwgdGhlbiBhIHNjcmlwdCB0aGF0IGxvYWRzIHBhY2thZ2VzLCByZWFkcyB0aGUgZGF0YSBhbmQgaW5zcGVjdHMgaXQuIFNhdmluZyBrZWVwcyB0aGUgcmVjb3JkIG9mIHdoYXQgeW91IGRpZC4=" data-hints="WyJUaGUgc2NyaXB0IGNhbm5vdCByZWFkIGEgZmlsZSB0aGF0IGlzIG5vdCBpbiB0aGUgcHJvamVjdCB5ZXQuIl0="}
Put the start of a new analysis in a sensible order, from first to last:

1. Read the data file into an object
1. Save the script with a clear name
1. Create an RStudio Project for the study
1. Look at the structure: rows, columns and types
1. Open a new script and load the packages at the top
1. Put the raw data file in the project's data folder
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="b1-09" data-world="b1" data-type="spot" data-diff="2" data-tags="projects,import" data-boss="1" data-hash="klczbj.5hvp6o" data-show="Rmxhd2VkOiAxLCAzLCA1" data-explain="MSBoYXJkLWNvZGVzIG9uZSBjb21wdXRlcidzIGZvbGRlciAodXNlIGEgUHJvamVjdCk7IDMgZGVzdHJveXMgdGhlIHJhdyBkYXRhIHlvdSBtYXkgbmVlZCBhZ2FpbjsgNSBsZWF2ZXMgbm8gcmVjb3JkIG9uY2UgdGhlIHNlc3Npb24gZW5kcyAod3JpdGUgYSBzY3JpcHQpLiAyLCA0IGFuZCA2IGFyZSBzb3VuZC4=" data-hints="WyJXaGljaCBhZHZpY2Ugd291bGQgbWFrZSB0aGUgd29yayBpbXBvc3NpYmxlIHRvIHJlcGVhdD8iXQ=="}
Boss: you are reviewing a colleague's first script. Flag every line of advice that is wrong.

- Putting setwd("C:/Users/Asha/Desktop") at the top makes the script run on any computer.
- Loading the packages at the top of the script makes its requirements clear.
- Saving the cleaned data over the original raw file keeps the folder tidy.
- Comments that explain why a step is done help the next reader.
- Typing commands only in the console is fine, because R keeps them for next time.
- read_csv() returns a tibble, which prints just the first rows and the column types.
:::
